blocks.content: The Constitution of India does not allow dual citizenship, that is, citizenship of India and citizenship of a foreign country simultaneously.

items: OCI cardholders do NOT possess voting rights in elections to Parliament or State Legislatures.
OCI cardholders cannot hold constitutional posts such as President, Vice-President, Supreme Court/High Court Judge, or Member of Parliament.
OCI cardholders are prohibited from purchasing agricultural or plantation properties in India.
Foreign citizens who were citizens of Pakistan, Bangladesh, or other notified countries cannot register as OCI cardholders.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) scheme was introduced by amending the Citizenship Act, 1955 in 2005.
The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2015 replaced the PIO and OCI cards with a single 'OCI Cardholder' category.
OCI cardholders enjoy a multi-purpose, multiple-entry lifelong visa for visiting India.
OCI status does not confer actual dual citizenship, as Article 9 of the Constitution prohibits dual citizenship.
Persons who have ever been citizens of Pakistan or Bangladesh are explicitly ineligible for OCI status.
